name: Old Ironjaw
lore: A great barracuda that has hung off the drop-off at Rocky Point for longer than the wreck has been on the reef. His lower jaw is crusted with the rust of other people's hooks.

clues.text: He hangs off the drop-off at Rocky Point, past where any island rod could reach.
In the full glare of the day, when the shadows are shortest.
Nothing dead and nothing slow. A spoon, worked fast enough to flash.
In the cool months, November to March, and never in the heat.

name: The Bishop
lore: A tarpon older than the town pier, silver gone to pewter, a scar across his gill plate. Port Esperanza has argued about him for forty years. Nobody has ever brought him to a boat.

clues.text: In the mouth of the Cut, where the bottom drops away to ink.
Only at dusk, when the water goes copper.
On the big tides: the days either side of a full moon or a new one.
He has refused every fly and feather ever thrown at him. A live sardine, or a big plug.
In the months the mangoes drop: June, July and August.

name: Old Gold
lore: A speckled peacock bass in his gold: the spots long gone, three bars as dark as charcoal, a hump on his head like a closed fist. Every low water the guides at Barcelos swear he has boiled under the fallen tree at the mouth of the lagoon, and every low water somebody's popper comes back with the hooks straightened.

clues.text: He lies under the fallen tree in the mouth of the lagoon, where the water goes deep.
In the heat of the day, when the sun is high. He doesn't stir for the dawn.
He wants noise on the surface. A big popper, chugged hard across the top.
As the water drops and then lies low, September to November, when the lagoon is cut off and crowded.
